questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, how many organs are there in the government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

According to the **Constitution of India**, there are three organs of government.

__
 
• These are the **legislature**, the **executive**, and the **judiciary**.
 
• The legislature refers to our **elected **representatives.
 
• The **executive** is a smaller group of people who are responsible for implementing laws and running the government.
 
• The **judiciary **refers to the system of courts in this country.
 
• To prevent the misuse of power by any one branch of government, the Constitution says that each of these organs should exercise different powers.

questions.question: Elements in the Modern Periodic Table are arranged in _______ vertical columns called groups and _______ horizontal rows called periods.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18,7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Henry Moseley **is the father of the modern periodic table.
 
• In 1913, Henry Moseley proved that an element's atomic number (abbreviated as **Z**) is a more fundamental property than its atomic mass.
 
• In the modern periodic table, elements are organised into **18 **vertical columns.
 
• Modern Periodic Law can be stated as the **physical** and **chemical** properties of the elements are periodic functions of their **atomic numbers**.
 
• Modern Periodic Table arranges the elements in the order of their atomic numbers in:
 
 
• **Seven horizontal rows (periods).**
 
• **Eighteen vertical columns (groups or families).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Each period begins with the filling of a **new** **energy shell**.
 
• In the modern periodic table, the first period is the shortest.
 
 
• **Hydrogen **and **Helium **are the elements in the first period.
 
 
 
• Elements are grouped in the modern periodic table in order of increasing atomic numbers, which is connected to their electrical configuration.
 
• The chemical reactivity of an element is determined by its location in the Periodic Table.
 
• Elements of group 18 of the modern periodic table are considered '**noble** **gas**'.

questions.question: Independence Day is celebrated at the national level at _______ in Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Fort**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Red Fort was constructed by **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638** as part of his new capital, Shahjahanabad (now Old Delhi).
 
• The fort is built in red sandstone and is a fine example of Mughal architecture, blending Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
 
• **In 2007,** the Red Fort was designated a** UNESCO World Heritage Site** for its historical and architectural significance.
 
• It served as the residence of Mughal emperors and is the site where the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag on Independence Day (August 15) every year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taj Mahal**

 
 
• The Taj Mahal was commissioned by **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1632** as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, **completed in 1648.**
 
• It is an outstanding example of Mughal architecture, combining elements of Persian, Indian, and** Islamic styles,** primarily built in white marble.
 
• The Taj Mahal was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983** and is recognized as one of the **Seven Wonders of the World**.
 
• The Taj Mahal is often referred to as a symbol of eternal love, as it was built to honor Shah Jahan’s beloved wife.
 
 
 
• **India Gate**
 
 
• India Gate was designed by **Sir Edwin Lutyens and inaugurated in 1931 **as a war memorial to honor the Indian soldiers who died during **World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.**
 
• The structure is **42 meters tall,** built in sandstone, and resembles the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.
 
• **In 1971, the Amar Jawan Jyoti **(Flame of the Immortal Soldier) was added under the arch to commemorate the soldiers who died in the **1971 Indo-Pak War.**
 
• India Gate is situated in New Delhi and forms a key part of the ceremonial avenue Rajpath, which hosts the Republic Day Parade every year.
 
 
 
• **Gateway of India**
 
 
• The Gateway of India was **built in 1924** to commemorate the visit of **King George V and Queen Mary to India in 1911.**
 
• It is designed in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style, combining elements of **Hindu and Muslim architecture,** and is made primarily of basalt.
 
• The Gateway of India is located in Mumbai, overlooking the Arabian Sea, and has historically served as a symbolic entrance to India for important dignitaries.
 
• The monument also marks the symbolic point where the last **British troops left India in 1948**, signifying the end of British rule after India's independence.

questions.question: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has appointed ________ as the chairman of the Senior Men's Cricket Selection Committee in 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajit Agarkar**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ajit Agarkar, a former Indian cricketer, was appointed as the **Chairman of the Senior Men's Cricket Selection Committee by the BCCI in 2023.**
 
• As Chairman, Agarkar oversees the selection of the Indian men's cricket team for international tournaments and matches, making key decisions regarding player selections.
 
• Ajit Agarkar brings valuable experience to the role, having represented India in **191 ODIs, 26 Tests, and 4 T20 Internationals**, making him a seasoned figure in Indian cricket.
 
• He succeeded Chetan Sharma, who held the position before him but resigned earlier in 2023.
 
• Agarkar’s appointment comes at a crucial time, ahead of major cricket tournaments like the **ICC Cricket World Cup 2023**, highlighting the importance of strong leadership in team selection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **M.S. Dhoni**

 
 
• M.S. Dhoni is the only captain in cricket history to have won all three major **ICC trophies: the T20 World Cup (2007), the ODI World Cup (2011), and the Champions Trophy (2013).**
 
• He led India to the number one position in the ICC Test rankings for the first time in 2009, cementing his legacy as a successful Test captain.
 
• Known as one of the best finishers in cricket, Dhoni has played numerous match-winning innings, particularly in limited-overs cricket, including the famous 2011 World Cup final, where he scored the winning runs.
 
• Dhoni has received several prestigious awards, including the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2007, and the Padma Bhushan in 2018**, recognizing his contribution to Indian cricket.
 
 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar**
 
 
• Sachin Tendulkar is the highest run-scorer in the history of both **Test and ODI cricket, with over 15,000 Test runs and 18,000 ODI runs.**
 
• He is the only cricketer to have scored **100 international centuries,** a unique record that sets him apart in both Tests and ODIs.
 
• Tendulkar was part of the Indian team that won the ICC Cricket World Cup in 2011, fulfilling a lifelong dream after representing India in six World Cups.
 
• He has been honored with several prestigious awards, including the** Bharat Ratna in 2014,** making him the first sportsperson to receive India's highest civilian award.
 
 
 
• **Kapil Dev**
 
 
• Kapil Dev captained India to its **first-ever ICC Cricket World Cup victory in 1983,** defeating the West Indies, marking a historic moment in Indian cricket.
 
• He is regarded as one of the greatest **all-rounders** in cricket history, becoming the **first player to achieve the double of 5,000 runs and 400 wickets in Test cricket.**
 
• Kapil Dev was India’s premier fast bowler in the 1980s and held the record for the most Test wickets (434) when he retired, surpassing Sir Richard Hadlee's record in 1994.
 
• He has been honored with the** Padma Shri (1982) and Padma Bhushan (1991)** and was inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame in 2010 for his contributions to cricket.

questions.question: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, industries in India have been classified into how many categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Three__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, industries were classified into three categories:** Schedule A, Schedule B, and Schedule C, **based on the level of government involvement in each sector.
 
• Industries under Schedule **A were considered critical for the national economy** and were reserved for the exclusive responsibility of the state. This included sectors like defense, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• Schedule **B industries were those where the state would play a dominant role**, but private sector participation was also allowed. Examples included chemicals, fertilizers, and machine tools.
 
• Industries under Schedule **C were left primarily to the private sector,** with the state stepping in only when necessary. This category included consumer goods industries.
 
• The 1956 Industrial Policy was a key document in laying the foundation for India’s socialist pattern of development, aiming for public sector dominance in key industries while allowing private participation in non-core sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The IPR of 1956 was introduced in the backdrop of **India’s post-independence economic scenario**, focusing on industrial development and self-reliance.
 
• The policy was aligned with the goals of the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, which emphasized rapid industrialization through public sector investment.
 
• The IPR encouraged the establishment of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to operate in key industries and promote economic growth.
 
• Role of Planning Commission: The Planning Commission played a crucial role in formulating the IPR, and setting guidelines for industrial development.
 
• The policy introduced a licensing system for setting up industries, requiring businesses to obtain licenses to regulate entry and ensure compliance with government goals.
 
• The IPR imposed restrictions on foreign investment and technology transfer to promote domestic industries and protect local interests.
 
• The policy prioritized the development of **heavy industries, such as steel and machinery,** to support overall industrial growth.
 
• The IPR recognized the importance of small-scale industries and encouraged their development through **policies, loans, and financial support.**
 
• The Industrial Policy aimed to generate employment opportunities through industrial expansion and promote balanced regional development.
 
• The IPR of 1956 underwent several amendments and updates over the years, culminating in **new industrial policies in the 1980s and 1990s to liberalize and modernize the Indian economy.**

questions.question: ATM booths come under which sector of the economic activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tertiary Sector**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ATM booths fall under the** tertiary sector as they provide essential financial services to customers,** facilitating banking transactions without the need for physical bank branches.
 
• They support the banking industry by offering convenience and accessibility, allowing customers to withdraw cash, check balances, and perform other **banking operations 24/7.**
 
• The operation and maintenance of ATM booths contribute to employment generation within the service sector, including roles in technology support, security, and customer service.
 
• By enhancing financial inclusion and promoting **digital transactions, **ATM booths play a significant role in the overall growth and efficiency of the economy, particularly in urban and semi-urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary sector**

 
 
• The primary sector involves the extraction and production of **natural resources,** including activities such as **agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining, and quarrying.**
 
• It serves as the foundation of the economy by providing raw materials for other sectors, particularly the secondary (manufacturing) and tertiary (services) sectors.
 
• The primary sector is a significant **source of employment,** especially in developing countries, where a large portion of the workforce is engaged in agriculture and related activities.
 
• Activities in the primary sector are heavily **dependent on natural conditions**, such as climate, soil fertility, and water availability, making it vulnerable to environmental changes and climate-related challenges.
 
 
 
• **Secondary sector**
 
 
• The secondary sector involves **transforming raw materials** from the primary sector into finished goods, such as textiles and automobiles.
 
• It contributes to the economy by adding value to raw materials, **significantly boosting GDP.**
 
• The sector provides substantial employment opportunities, often leading to urban migration and infrastructure development.
 
• It **drives industrialization,** enhancing productivity, innovation, and trade, thereby **supporting overall economic growth.**
 
 
 
• **Quaternary Sector**
 
 
• The quaternary sector **focuses on knowledge-based services**, including research and development (R&D), information technology, consulting, education, and financial services.
 
• It emphasizes the creation and management of intellectual capital, utilizing specialized knowledge and expertise to drive innovation and technological advancements.
 
• The sector plays a significant role in the economy by **contributing to GDP growth**, particularly in developed countries where service industries dominate.
 
• It generates** high-skilled employment opportunities**, often requiring advanced education and training, thereby supporting a skilled workforce and fostering economic development.

questions.question: Which state government launched the Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Scheme on Independence Day in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Rajasthan Chief Minister **Ashok Gehlot **will launch the Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Scheme on the occasion of Independence Day.
 
• Under the scheme, families covered under the National Food Security Act (**NFSA**) will get the Annapurna food packets every month from the fair price shops (FPS) for free.
 
• Each packet will contain **one kg** each of gram pulses, sugar and iodized salt, one litre soybean refined edible oil, 100 gram each of chili powder and coriander powder, and** 50 grams** turmeric powder
